problem: Data-driven demand-driven navigation (DDN) methods depend on pre-collected data and generalize poorly to unseen scenes and instructions. VLM-based navigators often need extra inputs (depth, multi-view, maps) and lack a mechanism to learn from their own failures.
motivation: Robots must find objects that satisfy implicit human needs (e.g. 'I am thirsty') without a given object list or known locations. Humans combine fast intuitive habits with slow deliberate analysis of errors. The authors argue that emulating this dual-process cognition with LLM/VLM reasoning gives better generalization from a single egocentric RGB view.
key_idea: A VLM-based DDN framework that pairs an SFT-tuned Heuristic Process (fast, CoT-based explore/exploit) with an Analytic Process that reflects on failures and writes corrected samples into a growing knowledge base used to fine-tune the Heuristic Process.
insight: Task-specific fine-tuning of the exploit policy matters: replacing it with vanilla GPT-4 drops NSR from 34.5 to 24.2 (single action) or 29.1 (sequence). CoT also matters: removing it drops NSR to 27.3. Iterating reflection over four rounds gives only marginal NSR/SSR gains but a large SPL gain, so reflection mainly teaches the agent to avoid obstacles and take more efficient paths. Most of the seen-to-unseen scene gap comes from 3D perception, not from the reasoning modules.
method: 3D Robot Perception: UniMODE detector trained on 55K AI2-THOR frames with 2D/3D box annotations, giving the object set in view.
Demand Matching: Qwen2-VL-7B fine-tuned with LoRA on 10.7K instruction-attribute QA pairs. It maps the instruction and detected objects to matched target objects and avoids over-generalized matches.
Knowledge Base: 72K expert trajectories from A* with GT target location; a VLM writes scene description, reasoning and decision (D, R, S) for each step, in a VQA format.
Heuristic Process, Explore: used when no object matches. GPT-4 with CoT outputs an action sequence from the current image, short-term action/rotation memory and an obstacle flag.
Heuristic Process, Exploit: used when a target is matched. Qwen2-VL-7B SFT on the knowledge base outputs description, reasoning and one action toward the target.

Analytic Process: on obstruction or failure, GPT with a reflection prompt analyzes the pre-failure state (description, reasoning, decision), produces corrected CoT and action, and adds it to the knowledge base for further SFT of the Heuristic Process.

setting.backbone: UniMODE (3D detector, trained) + Qwen2-VL-7B (LoRA SFT) for Demand Matching and Exploit + GPT-4 (frozen) for Explore and Analytic reflection
setting.training_data: 55K AI2-THOR frames (perception); 10.7K instruction-attribute pairs (demand matching); 72K A*-generated CoT trajectory samples plus reflection-corrected samples (heuristic)
setting.observation: single front-facing egocentric RGB view (no depth, no map) plus the text instruction; the perception module predicts 3D boxes from RGB
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 30°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT target location and A* paths used only to build training data)

numbers.eval_set_note: Unseen scene, unseen instructions (ProcTHOR test scenes, 485 test instructions); Table 1 text says 400 scenes
numbers.extra: single RGB view only; includes reflection; SFT on knowledge base

numbers_note: The DDN benchmark (AI2-THOR/ProcTHOR) is not in the canonical list, so it is labelled 'other'. The split labels for the four seen/unseen scene-instruction combinations are approximate. Table 1 has no separate val/test naming.
results: CogDDN reaches NSR 34.5 / SPL 17.1 / SSR 27.5 on unseen scenes and instructions, versus DDN's 16.1 / 8.4 / 6.0, about double the strongest single-view baseline. It also beats InstructNav (30.0 NSR / 14.2 SPL), which uses RGB plus depth.
limitations: Explore uses only short-term memory and has no long-term memory of visited areas.
Explore and reflection depend on GPT-4, which is expensive and impractical for real-world deployment.
The Heuristic Process must be re-fine-tuned whenever the knowledge base grows, which is inefficient. Evaluation is simulation-only.
